disclosures.name: TestWithDataIndependentTiming
disclosures.reason: The three Data Independent Timing (DIT) tests each begin by skipping when internal/cpu reports that the processor has no DIT feature. Go on Apple silicon, and on a linux arm64 processor whose HWCAP reports DIT, reports DIT and runs them: crypto/subtle.WithDataIndependentTiming sets the processor's PSTATE.DIT bit for the duration of the call, and the tests check that the bit is set inside it and restored after. The converted runtime cannot set that bit, because the .NET runtime exposes no control for PSTATE.DIT, so internal/runtime/sys reports DIT as unsupported and WithDataIndependentTiming leaves it unset. internal/cpu therefore reports HasDIT as false on an arm64 process, on darwin and on linux: the flag describes what the converted runtime can do, not what the silicon can do. Reporting it true would let WithDataIndependentTiming, and any caller that reads the flag, believe that DIT had been enabled when it had not. The converted side takes the skip branch the test's own source writes for a processor without DIT. On an Intel Mac and on linux-x64 both runtimes skip. Platforms darwin and linux (2026-11-12): the schema scopes an entry by GOOS only, with no architecture key, so the entry names linux; on an x64 process of either GOOS Go skips too and the entry is unused there. This entry retires when .NET gains a way to set PSTATE.DIT and the converted runtime uses it.
disclosures.history: Minted 2026-11-06 by C1 in the AES trio seat (claude/c1-aes-arm64), on COORD's ruling Q2 of the same day: HasDIT is held FALSE although Go's darwin osInit fills it from hw.optional.arm.FEAT_DIT, because a capability flag must describe what the converted runtime can do; .NET gives no way to set PSTATE.DIT (internal/runtime/sys/no_dit.cs: DITSupported false), and HasDIT=true would be a silent false security claim, worse than three honest reds. The divergence became visible when batch 208 moved the osx-arm64 oracle to native arm64 (-test-oracle-goarch), where Go's cpu.ARM64.HasDIT is true; under the earlier amd64 oracle (Rosetta) Go skipped too. Platform darwin: on osx-x64 both sides skip and the entry is unused there. The BOARD row (2026-11-06, C1) carries the retirement condition: a .NET API for PSTATE.DIT. Extended to linux 2026-11-12 by C1 (claude/c1-subtle-dit-linux), on COORD's ruling of that day, before S7 wave 2 dispatched the linux/arm64 bank: linux-arm64 clears HasDIT after Initialize (internal/cpu/linux-arm64/cpu_arm64_hwcap_impl.cs), under the same 2026-11-06 ruling, while Go on the arm runner reads it from HWCAP and runs the three tests, so without linux in scope they read as three new divergences there. The schema has no architecture key, so the scope is the GOOS; on linux-x64 Go skips as well and the entry never fires. The orphan check reports an entry only on a converted-side pass, so an unused entry is not an orphan on either x64 RID.
